spotTransfer.description: Σ spot-trade consideration and spot-market fees in this token: a transfer between the perpetual and the spot side, not perpetual PnL

seq.description: Raft log sequence number (the same axis as the write receipt's `seq` and the `x-dexos-seq` header)

symbol.description: Market symbol such as `BTC-USD` (perpetual) or `BTC-USDC` (spot); a merchant dex's markets carry its short code, `<code>:BTC-USD` (`:` may be sent as is or percent-encoded as `%3A`); case-insensitive

kind.description: Market type. A perp and a spot market may share a symbol; `symbol` + `kind` names exactly one market.

symbol.description: Market symbol such as `BTC-USD` (perpetual) or `BTC-USDC` (spot); a merchant dex's markets carry its short code, `<code>:BTC-USD` (`:` may be sent as is or percent-encoded as `%3A`); case-insensitive

A duplicate is `409 GatewayDuplicateClientOrderId`; the gateway reserves it atomically before sequencing and releases it if the request fails before sequencing. info.title: DEXOS Open API v1
info.summary: The standard public interface (REST + WebSocket) for builders, developers and liquidity providers
info.description:
The DEXOS public API for third-party developers, builders and liquidity providers. The specification
lives in `docs/specs/public-api-v1.md`; `docs/research/api-landscape-2026-09.md` compares it with
Hyperliquid, Lighter, Aster and Pacifica. **This document mirrors the gateway's v1 route table**
(`crates/gateway/src/api/v1.rs`, pinned by `scripts/check-openapi.mjs`, INV-API-V1-SPEC-MIRROR).
**Every read endpoint, write endpoint, vault endpoint and WebSocket channel listed here is implemented.**
The timestamp-window nonce shipped with the subaccount model v2 (`sigVersion: 2`, `docs/specs/subaccount-model.md`); the only planned item
is the builder volume projection (§6 of the specification).
The legacy endpoints (`/order`, `/markets`, `/ws`, …, documented at `/docs`) remain available; v1 is a
translation layer on top of them and returns bit-identical data.

## Quick start

1. `GET /v1/exchange` → the EIP-712 domain (`domain` / `chainId`) and the token table (with the numeric
   `token` ids the `Withdrawal` / `Transfer` structs carry); `GET /v1/markets/BTC-USD` → `priceDecimals` /
   `sizeDecimals` and `signingMarketId` (the `market` field of the signed structs).
2. `GET /v1/account/nonce?address=<your address>` → the next `nonce` and `signingAccountId` (the value for the
   `accountId` field of the signed struct; signing is the only thing it is for).
3. Scale `price` and `size` to integers locally (`ticks = price × 10^priceDecimals`,
   `lots = size × 10^sizeDecimals`), sign the `Order(...)` struct (each write endpoint states its
   `x-eip712.typeString`) and `POST /v1/orders`
   `{account, nonce, signature, symbol, side, type: "limit", price, size, clientOrderId?}` →
   `200 {orderId, status: resting|filled|…}` or `422 {error}`.
4. Programmatic trading: approve an API wallet once from the main wallet with
   `POST /v1/account/agents/approve`, then sign with it and pass its address as `signer`
   (the `AgentExec` signature covers the canonical-bytes hash of the inner command). Batch orders,
   cancels, replaces and the dead man's switch all go through the API wallet; **an API wallet cannot
   move funds**.
5. Subscriptions: `GET /v1/ws` → `{"method":"subscribe","params":{"channel":"book","symbol":"BTC-USD"}}`.
   After a disconnect, resume from the last `id` you saw with `/v1/account/fills?after=` or
   `/v1/events?after=`.

## Conventions

- Path prefix `/v1`; JSON; camelCase field names; timestamps in Unix milliseconds; lower-case enums.
- **Prices, sizes and amounts are decimal strings**: `ticks = price × 10^priceDecimals`,
  `lots = size × 10^sizeDecimals` (both must divide exactly); USDC amounts are scaled by `10^6`.
  `priceDecimals` / `sizeDecimals` come from `GET /v1/markets`.
- Markets are addressed by **`symbol`** (`BTC-USD` / `BTC-USDC`), accounts by **`address`**
  (+ `subaccount`, 0 = main account), vaults by **`vault`** (the vault id; v1.1 §4.3). **No v1 response addresses anything by a numeric id.** The numeric ids v1
  does return (`signingAccountId` on `/v1/account/nonce` and `/v1/account/subaccounts`, `signingMarketId` on
  `/v1/markets`, `token` on `/v1/exchange`) exist only because the EIP-712 structs carry them; they are inputs to
  signing, never addresses.
- Every error has the shape `{error:{code, num, message, details?}}`: `code` is a stable string
  (`Gateway*` for the gateway, the `CoreError` variant name for the execution layer), `num` a stable
  number (1xxxx gateway / 2xxxx execution layer). HTTP status: 400 malformed request · 401 bad
  signature · 403 ownership / scope · 404 · 409 · 412 replica behind · 421 wrong node · 422 business
  rejection · 429 rate limited · 5xx.
- Pagination: `?limit=&after=<cursor>` → `{…, next, hasMore}`; execution-history endpoints also
  return a fixed upper bound `upper`, which you pass back unchanged on the following pages.
- Read consistency: write receipts carry `x-dexos-seq`; a **read after a write** sends
  `x-dexos-min-seq` and gets 412 when the replica is behind (same semantics as the legacy API).

## Signing (write endpoints)

All write endpoints share one envelope: `{account, subaccount?, signer?, nonce, expiresAt?, signature,
…business fields}`. The signature is over the existing EIP-712 typed structs (each endpoint states its
`x-eip712.typeString`), with the domain from `GET /v1/exchange`. Prices and sizes inside the struct are
the **scaled integers**: the SDK scales locally and signs, the gateway performs the same scaling for its
pre-check, and the execution layer verifies the signature authoritatively. When `signer` is present the
request is signed by an API wallet (its nonce lives in the agent scope:
`GET /v1/account/nonce?address=&signer=`). API wallets can only trade; every fund-moving endpoint
answers `403 AgentScopeViolation`.

## Write receipts

By default (`ack=result`) the request waits for the fold (at most one epoch) and returns the business
outcome: a single order gets `200` with the order object or `422` with the rejection reason; a batch
always gets `200` with per-item `items[]`. `ack=sequenced` returns only `{seq, sub}` (for
high-frequency clients). If the outcome does not arrive within the budget the response is `202`:
**do not resend**; look it up with `GET /v1/requests/{requestId}`.

## Rate limiting

Two budgets, each a fixed 60-second window counted in request weights:

- **Per IP** — every `/v1/*` request. The IP is the TCP peer of the gateway; behind the deployment's own
  reverse proxy it is the `x-real-ip` that proxy writes. `x-forwarded-for`, and an `x-real-ip` sent by
  anyone other than a trusted proxy, are ignored.
- **Per account** — writes only, charged **after** the signature pre-check passes, keyed by the main wallet
  of the account being acted on (subaccounts share their main wallet's budget). A request that names
  someone else's address cannot pass the pre-check, so it never touches that account's budget.

Weights: reads 1, order book and prices 2, history endpoints 5, writes `1 + floor(n / 40)` where `n` is
the number of orders plus cancels in the request (a replace counts both). Both budgets default to 1200
per minute; the operator can raise either for a given IP or main wallet (market-maker tiers). Every
`/v1/*` response carries `ratelimit: limit=…, remaining=…, reset=…` and `ratelimit-policy: <limit>;w=60`
for the IP budget; a write that reached the account budget also carries
`x-ratelimit-account: limit=…, remaining=…, reset=…`. Exceeding either budget returns
`429 GatewayRateLimited` with `retry-after` and `details.bucket` = `ip` | `account`. API-wallet writes are
pre-checked at the gateway too: a signature that does not recover to `signer` is `401
GatewayBadSignature`; a `signer` with no grant on the account is `403 UnknownAgent`, an expired one
`403 AgentExpired` — none of them is sequenced. Right after approving an API wallet, send
`x-dexos-min-seq` = the approval receipt's `seq` with the first write. The legacy endpoints are not rate
limited (except `POST /subaccount`, which shares the IP budget).

post.summary: Fund a merchant dex insurance fund
post.description: The account owner signs a sigVersion 2 action whose inner command is `FundDexInsurance { account: placeholder, dex, amount }` (tag 0x8D); the amount moves from the account's withdrawable balance of the dex collateral token into the dex insurance account and counts as principal. API wallets get 403 `AgentScopeViolation`; dex 0 → 422 `InvalidDexConfig`. `token` (default USDC) only selects the decimals of `amount`. See `docs/specs/merchant-insurance-isolation.md` §4.1.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Dex id (≥ 1)

parameters.name: ack
parameters.description: Default: wait for the fold and return the business outcome; high-frequency clients use `sequenced` to get only `{status, seq, sub, requestId}`

403.description: Ownership / scope (an API wallet cannot move funds)

422.description: Business rejection (`code` = the CoreError variant name)

amount.description: Decimal amount of the dex collateral token

token.description: Token symbol or id; default USDC

servers.description: This gateway (the documentation page and the API share an origin)

x-error-codes.execution: `20000 + codec error code`; the code table is the CoreError numbering in `crates/core/src/codec.rs` (append-only); the string code is the variant name. Common ones: InsufficientMargin / NonceMismatch / SignatureExpired / AgentScopeViolation / MarketNotTrading / PostOnlyWouldCross / FokInsufficientLiquidity / ReduceOnlyWrongSide / OrderNotAligned / EquityTierLimitExceeded / InvalidLeverage / UnknownOrder / NotOrderOwner / SubaccountIndexMismatch / SubaccountLimitReached / AgentLimitReached / NonceOutOfWindow / UnknownAccount (sigVersion 2).

data.message: no such subscription on this connection

rules: Snapshot channels (book / bbo / prices / account / positions / orders) send one frame with `isSnapshot:true` on subscribe. book / bbo / prices / account / positions are then coalesced per block: events only mark them, and at each block boundary (`BlockBegun`, about once a second) each is read once and pushed only if its data changed (`isSnapshot:false`). account / positions of an account that holds positions are also re-read when marks or funding move, and those of any account whose ledger moved in the block (from the execution history's per-account ledger index — e.g. a vault redemption, whose events do not name the vault) are re-read at the block boundary (specification v1.1 §4.10-4).

Error frames answering a `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` carry the request `id` (when the request had one), `data.method` and `data.subscription` (the request's `params` verbatim), so a client can tell which request was refused. Unsubscribing a subscription the connection does not have is an error (`GatewayNotFound`), not `unsubscribed`. Error frames without `id` or `subscription` only answer malformed frames (specification v1.1 §4.10-3).

orders: the snapshot is all open orders across markets; after it every accept / fill / cancel / expiry is one frame with `clientOrderId` (if any) and `status` (open / filled / canceled / expired). Apply frames idempotently by `orderId`: a snapshot replaces the set, any other frame keeps the order if `status` is `open` and removes it otherwise. Order events already covered by the snapshot's view are not sent. `status` and `remaining` are always present: a taker's fill frames repeat the order's state at the end of the command (the same as its `accepted` frame); fills of protocol orders (liquidation, vault halt; `orderId` `"0"`, no `accepted`) are `filled` with `remaining` 0. When the connection cannot work them out it sends a fresh `isSnapshot:true` frame instead of an incomplete one. Pending conditional orders are part of the snapshot (rows with `trigger`); when one is placed, triggered, rejected or auto-cancelled a fresh snapshot is sent (those events carry no side / price / size), and cancelling one sends a `canceled` frame.

The candles channel sends one frame per fill with **the latest state of the current bar** (o/h/l/c/v accumulated; clients keep the last frame); a new bar starts automatically when the interval rolls over.

Time-series channels (trades / fills / ledger / events) carry `seq`; trades / fills / events send one frame per event with `data.id`, ledger one frame per command with `data.entries[]`. The fills `data.id`, and the last `data.entries[].id` of a ledger frame, are the `after` cursors of `/v1/account/fills` and `/v1/account/ledger`.

Resume: the subscribe ack carries the ledger `epoch` and the start position `seq`: every event after `seq` is sent on the subscription (unless a `lagged` follows); backfill time series up to `upper=<seq>-65535-4294967295` over REST and de-duplicate by `id` to join without gaps. Private frames carry `epoch` and `seq`, public book / bbo frames carry `seq`. `lagged{dropped, epoch, upper, reason}` means frames were not sent: `reason: buffer` = the server-side broadcast fell behind and `dropped` events were dropped; `reason: render` = the connection could not render time-series frames (execution history unreadable, market metadata missing; `dropped` is 0). **Frames not sent are never resent**. Right after it every snapshot subscription receives one `isSnapshot:true` frame, and fills / ledger frames at or before `upper` are no longer sent: backfill them with `after=<last id received>&epoch=<epoch>&upper=<upper>` (retry later on 400 `GatewayHistoryIncomplete`); the two parts join without gaps or duplicates. If `epoch` changed after a reconnect, rebuild state instead of resuming old cursors.
At most 200 subscriptions per connection; the server closes a connection that has sent no frame (pings count) for 60 s.

Rate limiting: REST uses fixed 60-second windows per IP and, for writes, per main wallet (weights: reads 1, order book / prices 2, history 5, writes 1 + floor(n / 40); default 1200 per minute each); every response carries `ratelimit` / `ratelimit-policy`, writes also `x-ratelimit-account`, and exceeding a budget yields 429 with `retry-after`. The WebSocket connection itself carries no weight.

Private channels (orders / fills / account / positions / ledger) accept `vault` instead of `address` / `subaccount` (specification v1.1 §4.3; giving both is an error frame); their frames then show `vault` in place of `address` / `subaccount`.

Channels that take `symbol` (book / bbo / trades / candles / funding) also take `kind` (`perp` | `spot`). A perp and a spot market may share a symbol; subscribing to such a symbol without `kind` is an error frame naming the choices (the gateway never picks one). Market frames carry `kind` next to `symbol`.

prices.data: `{prices:[Price], ts, window24h}` (same body as `GET /v1/prices`, including the 24h fields)

book.data: Book (`depth` levels per side, 1..=100, default 20, echoed as `depth`; out of range is an error frame). `aggTicks` as on `GET /v1/markets/{symbol}/book`: checked once when subscribing (a value outside the allowed set is an error frame listing the allowed values), echoed in every frame's `data`; the same symbol can be subscribed raw and at several `aggTicks` on one connection

trades.data: `{symbol, kind, id, price, size, side, ts}`

orders.data: Snapshot: `{address, subaccount, orders:[OpenOrder]}`. Update: `{address, subaccount, orderId, clientOrderId, symbol, kind, event: accepted|fill|canceled|expired, status: open|filled|canceled|expired, remaining, side?, price?, size?, filled?, lastFilled?, fillId?, ts}` (`status` and `remaining` always present)

candles.data: Candle (`{symbol, kind, i, t, T, o, h, l, c, v}`); the current bar is sent on every fill. `interval` takes the same values as REST; an unknown one is an error frame

funding.data: `{symbol, kind, rate, index, ts}`, one frame per funding settlement

ledger.data: `{address, subaccount, entries:[LedgerEntry]}` (or `{vault, entries}`): the `GET /v1/account/ledger` body without the paging tail, one frame per command with all of this account's entries in it, each identical to the REST entry. Read from the execution history's per-account ledger index — every entry the REST endpoint returns after the subscribe ack's `seq` is sent (vault deposits / redemptions, ADL and fee legs included)
